definitions.explanation: The Japanese comma (、), used to separate clauses and items in a sentence. One of the two basic punctuation marks in Japanese writing, alongside the period ({句点|くてん}).

examples.japanese: ここに{読点|とうてん}を{打|う}ってください。
{読点|とうてん}の{位置|いち}で{文|ぶん}の{意味|いみ}が{変|か}わることがある。
examples.english: The meaning of a sentence can change depending on where the comma is placed.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}の{作文|さくぶん}では、{読点|とうてん}と{句点|くてん}の{使|つか}い{分|わ}けに{気|き}をつけなければならない。
examples.english: In Japanese composition, you must be careful about the proper use of commas and periods.

notes:
USAGE:
The Japanese comma 、 is called {読点|とうてん}, while the period 。 is called {句点|くてん}. Together they are referred to as {句読点|くとうてん} (punctuation marks). The verb used for placing punctuation is {打|う}つ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {読点|とうてん}を{打|う}つ (to place a comma)
- {読点|とうてん}の{位置|いち} (comma placement)
- {句読点|くとうてん} (punctuation marks — commas and periods together)
